subject: maths
question: A man drove from home to a town at the speed of 60 km/hr and on his return journey, he drove at the speed of 30 km/hr and also took an hour longer to reach home. What distance did he cover each way?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **speeds** = 60 : 30 = 2 : 1

Since **distance** is constant, **Time ratio** = 1 : 2 (Inverse of speed ratio)

Difference in time ratio units = 2 − 1 = 1 unit

According to the question, 1 unit = 1 hour

Time taken for the first journey = 1 unit = 1 hour

**Distance** = Speed × Time = 60 km/hr × 1 hr = 60 km

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Outward Speed (S₁) = 60 km/hr

Return Speed (S₂) = 30 km/hr

Difference in time (Δt) = 1 hour

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/265611394903a6e8a5edb778b1724ad0e4e005db17a15d0d085b41f6263f76ef.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ − S₂) ] × Δt

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance = [ (60 × 30) ÷ (60 − 30) ] × 1

⇒ Distance = [ 1800 ÷ 30 ] × 1

⇒ Distance = 60 × 1

⇒ Distance = 60 km

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

When equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, **Average Speed** = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Speed-Distance-Time Relationship

Speed is directly proportional to **Distance** when Time is constant, and inversely proportional to **Time** when Distance is constant (S ∝ 1/T).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.</p
